text:
Help me write a cover letter. I've taught high school chemistry for 9 years and I'm applying to be a training coordinator at a pharmaceutical manufacturing plant about 30 minutes from me.

About me:
- I teach about 140 students a year across five classes.
- I wrote our school's lab safety program in 2019. Since then we've had no injuries in our labs that needed more than first aid.
- Our AP Chemistry pass rate went from 41% to 58% over the four years I've taught the course.
- Every year I train our new science teachers on lab procedures, about 12 hours each. There have been two a year on average.
- I've never worked in a regulated industry. The job posting asks for experience with GMP training records, which I don't have.
- I use Google Classroom. The plant uses a learning management system I haven't used.

I want the letter to say I can cut their new-hire training time in half. One page.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your answers will change what the letter says.

1. **What's behind "cut training time in half"?** Do you know how long their new-hire training takes now, or have you shortened a training program before? Unless you have something like that, a hiring manager will read it as a guess from someone who hasn't seen their program, and it could cost you credibility. A promise you can back up would be stronger, such as making training stick so people are ready sooner. If you do have evidence, tell me what it is and I'll use it.
2. **What's the company, the role title, and the hiring manager's name if you know it?** And besides GMP training records, what does the posting stress most? For example, onboarding, SOP training, compliance audits, or classroom vs. on-the-floor training.
3. **How did your lab safety program work?** Did it include written procedures, sign-offs or competency checks, records of who was trained on what, chemical inventory, or SDS management? Anything like that maps closely onto GMP documentation and would help cover that gap.
4. **What did you change in AP Chemistry to raise the pass rate, and what did the new-teacher training involve?** For example, did you write materials, check that teachers could do things on their own, or follow up with them? A sentence or two on each is enough.
5. **Why this move, and what are you doing about the gaps?** For example, are you taking a GMP course or learning their LMS (if you know which one it is)? Is there any other reason you want this job or this company?

If you don't know some of these, just say so. I'll write around anything missing rather than guess.

1. I don't know how long their new-hire training takes now. But in 2020 I rewrote our new-teacher lab training and cut it from 20 hours to 12. If I can't show I'd cut theirs in half, I'm fine saying what I did at the school instead.

2. Calder Pharmaceuticals, the plant in Westfield. The role is training coordinator. The posting names Karen Doyle as the HR manager. I don't remember the posting stressing anything else besides the GMP training records.

3. I keep a signed training record for every new teacher I train and for every student's lab safety quiz. The state has audited our lab safety records twice and found nothing. I don't have more detail on the rest of it for you.

4. I don't have specifics on the AP changes. For the new-teacher training, see #1: I rewrote it in 2020, and I keep a signed record for each teacher.

5. I've enrolled in an online GMP basics course that finishes May 2. I don't know which LMS they use. I don't have another reason to add.

I left out the "cut it in half" promise. You don't know how long Calder's training takes now, so the letter states what you've actually done (20 hours down to 12) and offers to look at their program the same way.

Dear Ms. Doyle,

I'm applying for the Training Coordinator position at Calder Pharmaceuticals. I've taught high school chemistry for nine years. Much of that work has been the job you're hiring for: training people to handle hazardous materials safely and keeping records that show they were trained.

In 2019 I wrote my school's lab safety program. Since then, our labs haven't had a single injury that needed more than first aid. I teach about 140 students a year across five classes. Every student takes a lab safety quiz, and I keep a signed record of each one. The state has audited our lab safety records twice and found no problems.

I also train every new science teacher on our lab procedures, about two a year. In 2020 I rewrote that training and cut it from 20 hours to 12. Each teacher signs a training record when they finish. I'd like to look at Calder's new-hire training the same way and find where it can be shorter and clearer.

Explaining hard technical material is the core of my work. In the four years I've taught AP Chemistry, our pass rate has risen from 41% to 58%.

I haven't worked in a regulated industry, and I haven't managed GMP training records. To close that gap, I've enrolled in an online GMP basics course that I'll finish on May 2. Much of my daily work already depends on the same habits as GMP: written procedures, documented training, and records that pass an audit. I haven't used your learning management system, but I run my classes in Google Classroom, and I expect to learn a new system quickly.

I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I could help train Calder's new hires. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
</invoke>
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send it:
- **The course date:** I wrote "May 2" without a year. If the course ends May 2, 2027, add the year if you want it to be clear the course is still in progress.
- **The AP paragraph:** It's short because I didn't have details on what you changed. If you remember one concrete change, adding it would make that paragraph stronger.
- **Length:** The letter is about 330 words, so it fits on one page with the address blocks.
